name: glTF Transform
role: Node CLI and library to inspect, optimise and compress glTF/GLB before a scene loads them
summary: Scriptable glTF 2.x toolkit: a CLI (`gltf-transform optimize`, `draco`, `meshopt`, `etc1s`/`uastc`, `inspect`) and a JS library with NodeIO. It runs in Node with no GUI and rewrites models, textures and animations into smaller, load-ready GLBs. In VCR it is a pre-production step that makes assets cheap for Three.js or Babylon.js to load; it renders nothing itself.
use_when: Shrinking a GLB (Draco/Meshopt, WebP/KTX2 textures) before a Three.js scene loads it
Scripted, repeatable asset prep in a build step; over Blender GUI export tweaks
Inspecting a model's meshes, materials, animations and sizes from the terminal
Over gltfjsx when you must rewrite the binary asset, not generate JSX
avoid_when: Authoring or rigging a model: Blender is the tool
Generating React components from a model: gltfjsx
Rendering anything: Three.js or Babylon.js load the output
KTX2 compression needs the external KTX-Software toolchain installed
notes: 2026-10-26: CLI docs say image work uses Sharp; KTX2 (etc1s/uastc) is assumed to need the KTX-Software binary, which is not verified here. Code licence read from npm metadata; the docs page itself is CC BY 3.0.

assessment.rationale: Regular 2026 releases on npm (4.4.2 July, 4.5.0 Sept 1, 4.5.1 Sept 28); MIT; headless Node CLI and API give a clear automation route. Nothing else in the catalogue does glTF optimisation.
